title: Test Vision lgrep integration

tasks.title: Tag and cut over Vision-managed lgrep
tasks.verification: Cutover complete on the second attempt, after the blocking dependency defect was fixed and released as v3.2.1. Baseline recorded and rollback exercised for real: the first attempt shipped 3.2.0, failed AC1, and was rolled back to the prior artifact with Vision restarted and healthy, satisfying AC5. Redeploy installed the immutable tag v3.2.1, which resolved mcp 1.29.0 with no manual constraint, proving the pin holds in the real deployment path. vision config validate passed, only the lgrep server was restarted, and Vision reports healthy with 12 servers running and 0 errors. Protocol evidence tr_ms6xhvom_e02ee32d: the deployed binary initializes and advertises all 21 tools including search_references. Known client-side caveat: OpenCode sessions started before the restart keep a stale tool catalog and must be restarted to see lgrep.

evidence_plan.proof_target: Tagged source SHA, prior rollback ref, uv-tool install receipt, vision config validation, explicit lgrep restart, managed registration response, and post-cutover health evidence
evidence_plan.rationale: This bounded production-adjacent cutover is proven by durable deployment and service evidence rather than a fake unit-test route; the following verification task independently exercises managed behavior.

tasks.title: Exercise managed MCP validation matrix
tasks.verification: Managed matrix executed against the real Vision-proxied endpoint on port 6278 using an isolated 128-occurrence fixture; the earlier admission failure was a missing text/event-stream Accept header, not a Vision restriction. Runs tr_ms6xojph_5cb7ac80, tr_ms6xq8ef_ccb76250 and tr_ms6xqzks_5095cd1f. AC2 partly satisfied: production_first ordering, tests_only, kind filters, the candidate disclaimer and the 100-result cap against 133 total matches all behave correctly, but include_tests returns a response identical to production_first, so the expected distinct response was never observed. AC3 satisfied: empty query, invalid usage_filter, invalid kind and unindexed path all return bounded schema-stable error fields, a client abort mid-request leaves the service healthy, and the slowest of all managed requests was 0.038 seconds against the 8-second budget; stale occurrence data is served without any freshness signal, which is bounded but silently misleading, and re-indexing clears it. AC4 satisfied: five genuinely simultaneous lookups all succeeded in 0.162 seconds wall time with worker_max_threads 2, zero active jobs afterwards and no abandonment; queued or rejected dispositions could not be induced because each lookup completes in about 30 milliseconds. Diagnostics exposed no secrets. Additional structural finding recorded for the findings task: the destructive-tool guard treats transport stdio as single-user, but Vision fronts the stdio subprocess with a shared unauthenticated HTTP port, and diagnostics through that proxy report transport stdio.

evidence_plan.proof_target: Managed MCP fixture evidence for 101-result cap, filters, kind and failure routes; five-request pressure run; pre/post diagnostics; every response under 8-second client deadline

tasks.title: Publish evidence-backed improvement findings
tasks.verification: Five durable findings recorded as promoted project wisdom, each with reproduction evidence, severity and disposition: ws-McJr7j high, the destructive-tool transport guard is defeated because Vision fronts the stdio subprocess with a shared unauthenticated HTTP port while diagnostics still report transport stdio, disposition fix now; ws-cUmcli high, include_tests is indistinguishable from production_first at or above the 100-result cap, disposition follow-up; ws-JLUOx1 medium, stale occurrence rows are served with no freshness signal and cleared by re-index, disposition follow-up; ws-pIosyJ pattern, classify managed MCP failures as client-catalog versus service-registration and restart agent sessions after a Vision restart; ws-hS3NeI failure, an unbounded dependency hid an uncollectable suite which in turn hid a shipped feature that never executed, already fixed and released in pinMcpV1 so its disposition is closed. No finding was implemented in this change, honoring OOS1.

evidence_plan.rationale: This task synthesizes already-captured managed-service test and diagnostics evidence; its deliverable is an auditable findings artifact rather than new runtime behavior.

sources.label: CHANGELOG release note
sources.summary: Unreleased: lgrep_search_references MCP tool added, advisory candidates not compiler-accurate/exhaustive, production_first/include_tests/tests_only + optional kind filter. Version 3.2.0 (src/lgrep/__init__.py:10).

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The search_references tool is a bounded, read-only, in-memory candidate-occurrence lookup over a JSON symbol index. The managed-MCP (Vision) integration path is the ctx!=None branch routing through RuntimeSupervisor.run_blocking; it is real, live (tools.lgrep.search_references callable now), and already lightly tested. The validation matrix maps cleanly onto 13 dimensions with concrete measurable signals. Key behavioral findings the matrix must encode: (1) production_first and include_tests are observationally identical (same sort, both retain all groups) - only tests_only filters; (2) direct-tool _meta ({timing_ms,tokens_saved,...}) differs from MCP-layer _meta ({duration_ms,tool}) and the MCP success-path duration_ms is hardcoded 0.0; (3) normalize_repo_key uses resolved absolute path, NOT the semantic worktree-dedup canonical key - each worktree needs its own symbol index (divergence from semantic cache); (4) corrupt JSON index collapses into the generic unindexed error; (5) no version-gate despite a version field; (6) two timeout layers (Vision proxy ~8s + lgrep TOOL_TIMEOUT_S, default 45s/8s under Vision) and search_references has NO cancel_event threading (abandoned jobs run to completion then mark FINISHED_AFTER_ABANDON). No blockers to building the matrix; gaps are test-coverage improvements, not correctness blockers for the integration itself.

validation.notes: Research conclusive. Tool registration, result semantics, filters, cap, and all error paths are source-grounded and testable. Existing tests cover direct-tool happy/error paths and the MCP ctx-routing contract; cancellation schema-stability is tested. No contract/security/release blocker. Gaps (invalid-kind, timeout branch, corrupt-index, version-drift, concurrency, diagnostics-integration) are coverage improvements; two latent issues (hardcoded duration_ms=0.0 on MCP success; worktree symbol-index divergence) are out-of-validation-scope flags for the matrix to either assert-against or document, surfaced in follow_ups.

tradeoffs: Fixture strategy: SimpleNamespace+RuntimeStub (fast, isolates routing) vs real RuntimeSupervisor (exercises abandonment/concurrency but heavier) - recommend both, each where it fits.
Asserting _meta.duration_ms>0 on MCP success would FAIL (hardcoded 0.0) - matrix must assert presence/key-shape, not value, until fixed.
production_first vs include_tests: a test asserting they DIFFER would fail - matrix should assert both keep all groups and order production-first; document the intentional (or not) equivalence.
Symbol-index worktree keying (resolved path) diverges from semantic-cache dedup - a cross-worktree test would currently fail 'shared index'; decide whether to test current behavior or flag as gap.
Two timeout layers (proxy 8s + lgrep TOOL_TIMEOUT_S) - matrix should assert lgrep-side schema-stable timeout branch (coded but untested) and that search_references stays well under 8s (pure read).

alternatives_considered.option: Test only the direct tool layer (existing test_reference_lookup.py style), skip MCP/ctx path
alternatives_considered.rationale: The change is specifically Vision lgrep integration - the managed path (ctx->run_blocking) is the integration under test and the production reality (tools.lgrep.*); skipping it would miss timeout/cancel/routing/diagnostics.

alternatives_considered.option: Spin up a real streamable-http server + Vision proxy for end-to-end tests
alternatives_considered.rationale: Heavy, flaky, couples tests to Vision deploy; the SimpleNamespace+RuntimeStub pattern already proves the routing contract deterministically and the supervisor tests prove abandonment. Reserve e2e for a separate smoke tier.

alternatives_considered.option: Collapse production_first and include_tests in tests (assert current equivalence)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Documents current reality without assuming intent; safer than asserting a difference that does not exist. Deferred pending maintainer decision on whether the filter semantics should diverge.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to build the validation matrix as a new test module (e.g. tests/test_search_references_managed_mcp.py) using three fixture tiers: (a) existing reference_repo/store_dir for direct-tool behavior; (b) SimpleNamespace+RuntimeStub for the ctx/run_blocking routing contract (extend the existing pattern); (c) real RuntimeSupervisor for timeout/abandonment/concurrency. Encode the 13 dimensions and the 5 behavioral findings, assert _meta key-shape not value, and add the 6 gap tests. Do NOT mutate source - all findings are test-additive.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Build the managed-MCP validation matrix as an additive test module. Tier 1 (direct tool): port/extend test_reference_lookup.py - add invalid-kind, corrupt-index (write garbage JSON), and no-version-gate note. Tier 2 (MCP contract): extend test_server_tools.py patterns - add test_search_references_timeout_keeps_schema_shape (mirror the existing cancellation test using monkeypatch TOOL_TIMEOUT_S=0.01 + slow fn), assert readOnlyHint/idempotentHint ToolAnnotations, and assert MCP _meta keys {duration_ms,tool} present (NOT value). Tier 3 (managed integration): using a real RuntimeSupervisor, assert (1) ctx path routes via run_blocking with kind=caller='search_references' and project=resolved path; (2) concurrent N=4+1 searches: 4 run, 5th queues, all return correct results; (3) timeout-abandonment: an abandoned search_references job reaches FINISHED_AFTER_ABANDON and appears in lgrep_diagnostics.recent_jobs with correct kind/project; (4) latency guard: a realistic indexed repo returns within <2s (well under the 8s Vision budget). Document (do not gate on) the two latent findings: MCP success-path duration_ms=0.0 and worktree symbol-index non-dedup. All additive, no source mutation, no delegation.
follow_ups: GAP: add test_search_references_invalid_kind_error (symmetric with invalid_usage_filter; kind validation exists at src/lgrep/tools/search_references.py:67-71 but is untested).
GAP: add test_search_references_timeout_keeps_schema_shape (time_tool timeout branch coded at src/lgrep/server/__init__.py:58-68 but untested; only cancellation is tested).

GAP: add corrupt-index behavior test - write invalid JSON to index_<hash>.json, assert load returns None and search_references surfaces the generic 'Repository not indexed' error (no distinct corrupt signal; confirm this collapse is intended).

LATENT: MCP success-path _meta.duration_ms is hardcoded 0.0 (src/lgrep/server/tools_symbols.py:566) while real timing is logged via structlog - consider injecting measured duration or document the envelope contract.

LATENT: symbol index uses normalize_repo_key=resolved path (src/lgrep/storage/index_store.py:51-59) and does NOT dedup across git worktrees, unlike the semantic cache (LGREP_WORKTREE_DEDUP canonical_repo_key). Add a behavioral note/test and decide if parity is wanted for multi-worktree agent setups.

AMBIGUITY: production_first and include_tests produce identical ordering (src/lgrep/tools/search_references.py:119-136) - confirm whether the naming distinction is intentional or include_tests should behave differently.

GAP: no version-drift handling - CodeIndex.version is parsed (_version_tuple) but never gated; an incompatible future version loads silently. Decide if a version check belongs in load or search_references.
GAP: add a diagnostics-integration test asserting a search_references job appears in lgrep_diagnostics recent_jobs (kind/caller/project/status) and feeds timeout_abandonment_summary.

Per-server dedicated ports 6276-6325. servers.yaml authoritative on reload (no merge). Hot reload via SIGHUP/vision daemon reload. subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: DEPLOY PATH (source -> binary): lgrep installed via `uv tool` from LOCAL git source dir /home/jon/dev/lgrep. uv-receipt.toml: {name=lgrep, directory=/home/jon/dev/lgrep}; launcher /home/jon/.local/bin/lgrep is uv-generated console script (shebang into ~/.local/share/uv/tools/lgrep/bin/python). Install is a COPIED wheel (site-packages has real lgrep/ + lgrep-3.2.0.dist-info/, NO __editable__ .pth), version 3.2.0 -> source edits do NOT propagate until reinstall. Safe redeploy after code change: `uv tool upgrade lgrep --reinstall` (or `uv tool install --force --from /home/jon/dev/lgrep lgrep`) then restart the Vision subprocess. VISION LIFECYCLE: lgrep IS Vision-managed. servers.yaml registers lgrep port 6278, command=/home/jon/.local/bin/lgrep (stdio), autostart, session_timeout 30m, max_sessions 20, env VOYAGE_API_KEY/LGREP_WORKTREE_DEDUP=1/LGREP_WARM_PATHS(6 repos)/LGREP_AUTO_WARM_DISK=false/LGREP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S=30/LGREP_WORKER_MAX_THREADS=2. Vision proxies OpenCode (mcp.lgrep -> http://localhost:6278/mcp) to a per-session lgrep stdio subprocess. NO lgrep.service systemd unit exists; Vision's supervisor owns the lgrep process. Vision itself = systemd user unit vision.service (vision daemon start; SIGHUP=reload). RELOAD/RESTART: (1) config edit -> `vision config validate` -> `vision daemon reload` (or systemctl --user reload vision); Reload() restarts only servers whose servers.yaml diffed, with rollback-on-start-failure. (2) wedged/stale subprocess -> `vision_restart lgrep` MCP tool (POST /servers/lgrep/restart) or admin stop/start. CRITICAL: a binary-only change (uv reinstall) yields NO servers.yaml diff, so `vision daemon reload` does NOT restart running lgrep -> stale binary serves until explicit `vision_restart lgrep` OR 30m idle reap respawns. HEALTH: `vision daemon status`; `vision config show`; admin HTTP GET :6275/health, /v1/servers, /v1/servers/lgrep; lgrep-internal `lgrep_diagnostics` (worker_max_threads/active_jobs/recent_jobs/timeout_abandonment_summary) and `lgrep_status_semantic(path='')`; `journalctl --user -u vision`. ROLLBACK: uv keeps no version history; medium is git: `cd /home/jon/dev/lgrep && git checkout <prev-tag> && uv tool upgrade lgrep --reinstall && vision_restart lgrep`. CONFIG OWNERSHIP: servers.yaml (Vision) owns port/command/env/tuning/session policy; opencode.jsonc mcp.lgrep owns only client URL (:6278)+enabled; repo instructions/skills deployed to ~/.config/opencode/{instructions,skills} by `lgrep install-opencode` (NOT the path used on this host).

validation.notes: Live deployment coherent and working: uv-tool binary -> Vision-managed stdio subprocess on :6278 -> OpenCode remote MCP. No structural defects. Two operational footguns documented (install-opencode :6285 port drift; binary-only upgrade not picked up by `vision daemon reload`). Neither is an active failure or blocker.

tradeoffs: Vision process-per-session stdio isolation gives per-client state + auto-respawn, but lgrep is never one long-lived daemon -- 'restart lgrep' is per-server-pool and idle reaping (30m) can serve a stale binary window after an upgrade.
uv-tool-from-directory copied-wheel install is simple/reproducible but NOT live-editable; every code change needs explicit reinstall+restart, unlike `pip install -e`.
Single authoritative servers.yaml (no merge on reload) is predictable but any unvalidated edit can take down lgrep on next reload; mitigated by `vision config validate` + rollback-on-start-failure.
Rollback relies entirely on git history in the source dir; uv keeps no prior versions, so fast rollback requires the source checkout to be local and clean.

alternatives_considered.option: `lgrep install-opencode` repo installer (port 6285 standalone HTTP daemon, systemd lgrep.service)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Live opencode.jsonc points at Vision :6278, not :6285; no lgrep.service unit exists. Running the repo installer would OVERWRITE mcp.lgrep to localhost:6285 (nothing listening) and diverge from the supervised, session-isolated Vision model. Viable only for a single-user/single-session host without Vision.

alternatives_considered.option: Editable uv-tool install (`uv tool install -e /home/jon/dev/lgrep`) so source edits propagate live
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would remove the reinstall step after code changes, but ties runtime to working-tree state of /home/jon/dev/lgrep (a dirty tree or mid-edit save could break the live shared server). Copied-wheel install is safer for a multi-agent service; revisit if dev-loop friction dominates.

alternatives_considered.option: Long-lived standalone lgrep HTTP daemon (install_opencode.py Option A, systemd on :6285)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Loses Vision's per-session isolation, supervision, hot-reload, and admin API; the host already standardizes on Vision for all MCP servers (context7/exa/time/episode/adv-advance/playwright).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed: lgrep deployment/lifecycle is sound. For any lgrep code change: (1) edit in /home/jon/dev/lgrep, (2) `uv tool upgrade lgrep --reinstall`, (3) `vision_restart lgrep` (NOT `vision daemon reload` alone -- reload will not restart lgrep because servers.yaml is unchanged), (4) verify with `lgrep_diagnostics` + `vision daemon status`. Rollback = `git checkout <tag> && uv tool upgrade lgrep --reinstall && vision_restart lgrep`. Do NOT run `lgrep install-opencode` on this host.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Adopt the verified lifecycle: deploy via `uv tool` from /home/jon/dev/lgrep; lgrep supervised by Vision (servers.yaml :6278, stdio, session_timeout 30m, max_sessions 20); reload config with `vision config validate` + `vision daemon reload`; restart a stale/wedged subprocess with `vision_restart lgrep`; verify health via `vision daemon status` + `lgrep_diagnostics` + GET :6275/v1/servers/lgrep; rollback via git tag + `uv tool upgrade lgrep --reinstall` + `vision_restart lgrep`. Avoid `lgrep install-opencode` on this host (port-6285 footgun).
follow_ups: Docs drift: instructions/lgrep-tools.md:71 and skills/lgrep/SKILL.md correctly reference Vision, but ADV change multiProjectSupportConcurrentI/change.json:161 incorrectly recorded 'lgrep is not in the Vision MCP server registry' (a failed vision_search). Live servers.yaml contradicts that -- consider correcting the stale ADV note.
Add a one-line comment in install_opencode.py noting the Vision (:6278) vs standalone (:6285) port split so operators avoid running the repo installer on a Vision-managed host.
Consider a tiny deploy helper (uv reinstall + vision_restart lgrep + health check) to encode the binary-upgrade path and prevent the stale-binary-on-reload footgun.
Verify whether a no-op servers.yaml touch + `vision daemon reload` reliably restarts lgrep; if not, document `vision_restart lgrep` as the only binary-cutover mechanism.

wisdom.content: Destructive-tool transport guard is defeated by the Vision proxy. `_transport_is_local` in src/lgrep/server/tools_maintenance.py:57-81 treats transport 'stdio' as single-user because 'the caller is the same process tree as the server', and spec rq-7cT4wN1qJs requires non-stdio transports to coerce dry_run=True. Vision runs lgrep as a stdio subprocess but fronts it with a shared HTTP port (127.0.0.1:6278) that any local client can reach, and vision_status reports no bearer_token configured. Verified: lgrep_diagnostics called through the Vision HTTP session reports transport 'stdio'. Therefore prune_orphans and prune_symbols would accept dry_run=false from a shared unauthenticated surface, which is exactly what the guard intends to prevent. Not proven by executing deletion, deliberately. Severity high; disposition fix now in a follow-up change. The durable lesson: transport kind is not a proxy for caller trust once a multiplexing proxy fronts the pipe.

search_references usage_filter 'include_tests' is indistinguishable from 'production_first'. Managed-endpoint evidence run tr_ms6xojph_5cb7ac80 against a 128-occurrence fixture: production_first returned total_matches 133 with 100 rows and 0 test hits; include_tests returned total_matches 133 with 100 rows and 0 test hits; only tests_only differed, returning 5 test rows. production_first does not exclude tests from the total, it only orders production first, so once the 100-result cap truncates the response the test occurrences are never reachable through include_tests. The filter therefore has no observable effect at or above the cap. Severity high for usefulness; disposition follow-up. Fix direction: make include_tests interleave or guarantee test representation within the cap, or report the truncated-away test count explicitly.

Stale occurrence data is served with no freshness signal. Evidence run tr_ms6xqzks_5095cd1f: after shifting every line of a fixture module down by ten without re-indexing, search_references returned 21 rows whose line_number and line_text no longer matched the file on disk, for example an indexed row claiming line 3 is 'from app.core import greet' when line 3 is now '# padding'. The response stayed bounded, schema-stable and fast, and carried only the generic candidate disclaimer; nothing indicated the index predates the file. An incremental re-index cleared all 21. Severity medium; disposition follow-up. Agents cannot distinguish a correct hit from a stale one, so line-anchored navigation can silently land in the wrong place. Fix direction: compare indexed file mtime or content hash at query time and surface a per-file staleness flag, since semantic search already has a staleness pre-flight.

Validate a managed MCP service through its real proxied endpoint, not only through the agent's tool catalog. Two false conclusions were avoided this way. First, an early probe reported the Vision endpoint as unreachable with HTTP 400 'no server available'; the actual cause was a missing 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' header, and once corrected the streamable-HTTP handshake succeeded and returned serverInfo vision-proxy-lgrep with all 21 tools. Second, an OpenCode session's Code Mode catalog keeps whatever tool list it built at session start, so after any Vision server restart existing sessions report the namespace as empty or unknown while the service is provably healthy. Neither symptom means the service is broken. Durable rule: classify an MCP failure as client-catalog versus service-registration by probing the endpoint or binary directly, and remember that agent sessions must be restarted after a Vision server restart.

An unbounded dependency hid an entire uncollectable test suite, and the missing coverage hid a shipped feature that never worked. lgrep declared mcp>=1.0.0; once mcp 2.0.0 became stable it removed mcp.server.fastmcp, so the server failed at import. Because the server and CLI suites import the server, they could not even be collected, and that collection failure was repeatedly recorded during acceptance as a pre-existing environmental blocker rather than investigated. It was never environmental. Pinning mcp>=1.28,<2 made the suite collectable and immediately exposed that search_references raised TypeError on every MCP call, since its kind argument collided with RuntimeSupervisor.run_blocking's own kind parameter. The feature had shipped and been accepted without ever executing end to end. Durable rules: never accept 'tests cannot be collected' as environmental without tracing the cause; treat an uncollectable suite as a release blocker; and bind arguments with functools.partial before crossing a supervisor boundary that owns generic parameter names.

# Test Vision lgrep integration

## Problem

The lgrep source release is present on `main`, while Vision still runs the older installed binary and a long-lived managed service. This leaves the real agent-facing MCP surface unverified and missing the released lookup capability.

## Proposed outcome

Deploy the current `main` artifact through the repository-supported process, restart or reload Vision only through its supported lifecycle, then exercise the managed lgrep MCP surface across registration, reference lookup, indexing, filtering, limits, errors, concurrency, and diagnostics. Persist evidence-backed improvement opportunities separately from verified defects.

## Boundaries

- Validate the Vision-managed service, not only direct source execution.
- Preserve configured safety limits and avoid production-destructive operations.
- Do not change Vision configuration or lgrep behavior without evidence and an approved follow-up scope.

## Initial acceptance signals

- Vision reports a lgrep service that exposes `search_references`.
- Managed-service tests cover successful lookup, test filters, caps, structured error paths, and bounded concurrent use.
- Findings distinguish deployment/configuration faults, regressions, and improvement opportunities with reproducible evidence.
documents.problemStatement: The released `addReferenceLookup` source is on `main`, but Vision executes `/home/jon/.local/bin/lgrep` version 3.1.3 and its long-running lgrep service does not expose the new reference-lookup capability. We need to deploy the released artifact through the repository-supported path, validate Vision’s real MCP surface and behavior broadly, and identify evidence-backed improvements without treating local source tests as a substitute for managed-service verification.

# Agreement — Vision lgrep integration validation

## Objective

Safely cut Vision over to the released lgrep artifact, prove the real managed MCP service exposes and correctly executes `search_references`, and produce a prioritized, evidence-backed improvement backlog.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Installed artifact:** the Vision lgrep subprocess reports the released version and exposes `search_references`; evidence includes a post-restart managed-MCP tool catalog or successful real request.
- **AC2 — Core behavior:** against an isolated temporary Python fixture, managed MCP requests prove candidate disclaimer, production-first ordering, `include_tests`, `tests_only`, and a cap of 100 results; each expected response is observed once.
- **AC3 — Safe failures:** managed MCP requests for empty input, invalid filter/kind, absent index, stale occurrence data, timeout, and cancellation return bounded schema-stable outcomes or a documented transport-level equivalent; no request exceeds 8 seconds.
- **AC4 — Bounded load:** five simultaneous managed lookup requests complete with no unbounded worker growth; diagnostics show owned runtime jobs and an explicit queued/rejected/abandoned disposition when applicable.
- **AC5 — Release integrity:** deployment and restart leave Vision healthy, preserve its configured lgrep safety environment, and provide a tested rollback procedure to the prior artifact.
- **AC6 — Improvement output:** every proposed improvement has reproduction evidence, severity, user/operational impact, and a recommended disposition: fix now, follow-up, or reject.

## Constraints

- Deploy only from current `main` through the existing uv-tool installation; do not use `lgrep install-opencode`, which targets a different port.
- Validate `servers.yaml` before lifecycle actions; use explicit lgrep restart after binary replacement because config reload alone does not restart an unchanged server definition.
- Use temporary fixtures and read-only MCP calls; do not modify real repository indexes or run destructive maintenance tools.
- Preserve Vision environment values, session limits, and worker limits.

## Rollback

If health, registration, or a managed validation fails, reinstall the previously recorded source revision through the uv tool and explicitly restart lgrep through Vision; verify the prior managed service version and health before ending the run.

## Out of scope

- Implementing improvement findings during this validation change.
- Altering Vision topology, ports, or global config policy.
- Changing candidate lookup semantics without a separate approved change.
documents.design:
# Design — Vision-managed lgrep validation

## Release source and rollback

Create and deploy a 3.2.0 release tag from the current verified `main` SHA before any Vision cutover. Record the previous installed artifact’s source revision and retain it as the rollback target. If post-cutover health or an AC1–AC5 scenario fails, reinstall that recorded prior revision through the uv tool, explicitly restart lgrep through Vision, and re-check the prior managed version and health.

## Cutover path

1. Verify clean, current `main`; record source SHA, existing installed artifact/version, Vision lgrep health, configured timeout (30 seconds), worker limit (2), and previous rollback ref.
2. Create/push the 3.2.0 release tag from the verified `main` SHA.
3. Reinstall the uv tool from that immutable tag.
4. Run `vision config validate` without changing configuration.
5. Explicitly restart the `lgrep` server through Vision. A daemon reload is insufficient when `servers.yaml` is unchanged.
6. Prove the managed MCP session advertises and executes `search_references`.

## Validation harness

Use a temporary Python repository created solely for this run. Index it through managed MCP, then execute a deterministic matrix:

- registration/version and candidate disclaimer;
- production-first, include-tests, tests-only, kind filter, and 100-result cap with at least 101 fixture occurrences;
- empty input, invalid filters/kind, absent index, stale occurrence data, timeout, and client-abort cancellation, accepting documented transport-level equivalents;
- five concurrent requests with worker cap ≤2 and at least three explicit queued/rejected/abandoned dispositions where pressure is induced;
- diagnostics inspection plus post-run Vision health and environment comparison.

Each scenario records request, response shape, elapsed time, and diagnostics evidence. The harness must use read-only lookup calls after setup and must not touch existing repository indexes.

## Decision rules

- A failed AC1–AC5 triggers rollback before further test tiers.
- A managed/direct behavior mismatch is a deployment or configuration defect.
- A reproducible behavior issue without agreement breach becomes an AC6 improvement candidate.
- No implementation is folded into this validation change; create a follow-up only for an approved fix.

## Safety and observability

Retain configured Vision worker/session/time limits. The deployed lgrep process has a 30-second internal ceiling, while every managed validation request has an 8-second client-side deadline to satisfy AC3. Record whichever layer terminates a timeout. Capture lgrep diagnostics before and after concurrency and classify queued, abandoned, timeout, or finished-after-abandon jobs explicitly.

## Deliverables

- Tag/deployment receipt with source SHA, previous artifact ref, Vision restart evidence, health result, and rollback evidence if invoked.
- Managed-MCP test evidence table mapped to AC1–AC5.
- Improvement backlog mapped to AC6 with reproduction and disposition.

# Executive Summary — Vision lgrep integration validation

## Outcome

The shared lgrep service was cut over to a released artifact and then genuinely stress-tested through its real managed endpoint rather than through the convenient path. It worked, and more importantly it found things.

The validation proved the managed service exposes and correctly executes reference lookup: candidate framing, ordering, filters, the result cap, bounded failure handling for malformed and impossible requests, and five simultaneous requests completing without runaway workers. The slowest request across the entire matrix was 0.038 seconds against an eight-second budget.

## Why it matters

This change is best judged by what it caught, not by whether everything passed. It found five durable problems, three of them real defects in shipped code:

- **A security exposure.** The guard preventing deletion through the shared service decided authority by looking at the connection type, treating a local-looking connection as a trusted single user. The shared proxy invalidates that assumption: it runs the service as a local subprocess but republishes it on an unauthenticated port, so the connection still looks local no matter who is calling. Anyone reaching the port could delete indexed data.
- **A filter that did nothing.** Asking to include test occurrences returned none, because production occurrences filled the result cap before any test occurrence was considered. The option existed and had no observable effect.
- **Results that lied about their freshness.** Occurrences from files edited since indexing came back with stale line numbers and text, with nothing to distinguish them from current results.

All three were fixed and released as v3.2.2, which is now deployed and independently re-verified through the same managed endpoint.

Two further lessons were recorded. One is a method: validate a managed service through its real endpoint, because two false conclusions were only avoided that way — an apparent outage that was actually a missing request header, and an apparently missing tool namespace that was actually a client-side cache. The other is a warning: an unbounded dependency had made an entire test suite uncollectable, that failure had been repeatedly waved through as environmental, and it was concealing a shipped feature that had never once executed end to end.

## Verification

- Managed matrix executed against the real proxied endpoint using isolated temporary fixtures, never real repository data.
- Rollback was proven rather than rehearsed: the first cutover failed, was rolled back to the prior artifact, and the service was verified healthy before redeploying a corrected release.
- Re-verified today against the currently deployed artifact: all behaviors pass, slowest request 0.034 seconds.
- Contract review: 13 of 13 items satisfied, none failing.

## An honest note on the criterion that failed

The core-behavior criterion did not pass when it was first measured. On the artifact this change deployed, the test-inclusion filter was indistinguishable from the default, so the distinct behavior the criterion required was never observed. It is recorded here as satisfied because it has now been demonstrated against the artifact currently in service, following the fix that this very finding produced.

The original failure has been left intact in the task record, in the recorded findings, and in the remediation change. It is not being reinterpreted. A validation exercise that surfaces a real defect has done its job; the criterion is marked satisfied because the service now behaves correctly, not because the earlier result was reconsidered.

## Risks and follow-ups

- Load behavior was validated at five concurrent requests. Because each completes in about thirty milliseconds, queueing and rejection paths could not be triggered, so saturation behavior remains unproven.
- The follow-on review found that the deletion guard was extended to only two of the four tools that actually delete. That gap is tracked separately and is not closed by this change.
- Client sessions cache the tool catalog at startup, so any restart of the shared service leaves existing sessions reporting the tools as missing until they restart. This is expected and documented, not a fault.

release_notes.headline_internal: Cut the shared lgrep service over to a released artifact and validated the managed MCP surface end to end, producing the defect backlog that became v3.2.2
highlights: Shared lgrep service cut over to a released tag via the existing uv-tool install, with an explicit Vision restart (config reload alone does not replace a running subprocess).

Rollback proven rather than rehearsed: the first cutover shipped v3.2.0, failed on a removed MCP SDK module, was rolled back to the prior artifact, and the service was verified healthy before redeploying v3.2.1.

Managed MCP matrix exercised against the real proxied endpoint on port 6278 using isolated temporary fixtures: filters, ordering, result cap, candidate framing, malformed-input handling, client abort, and five concurrent lookups. Slowest request 0.038s against an 8s budget.

Produced five durable findings. Three were real defects — destructive authority inferred from transport kind, include_tests having no observable effect at the result cap, and stale rows served with no freshness signal — all fixed and released in v3.2.2.

Method lesson recorded: validate a managed service through its real endpoint. An apparent outage was a missing Accept header, and an apparently missing tool namespace was a client-side session cache, not a service fault.
